function.description: This function is used to create a recommendation model using a given user data and an algorithm type Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_data.description: A data frame of user ratings. Rows represent users, columns represent items, and entries represent user ratings for items

algorithm.description: The algorithm to be used for creating the recommendation model. Collaborative filtering, content-based filtering and hybrid filtering.

matrix_factorization.description: Optional parameter to indicate whether matrix factorization should be used. Default is False.

Below is a practical, step‑by‑step guide you can follow to build a modern, scalable frontend for an e‑commerce site. I’ll cover the whole pipeline—from planning and design to coding, testing, and deployment—so you can pick the parts that fit your team’s skill set and project constraints. --- ## 1️⃣ Planning & Requirements | Item | Why it matters | How to do it | |------|----------------|--------------| | **Business goals** | Determines which features matter most (e.g., product catalog, cart, checkout, reviews). | Interview stakeholders; write a short “feature backlog.” | | **Target audience** | Influences design style, accessibility needs, and device mix. | Create personas; note device usage stats. | | **Performance targets** | E‑commerce sites must load fast to reduce cart abandonment. | Set metrics: First Contentful Paint < 2 s, Time to Interactive < 5 s. | | **Compliance** | GDPR, PCI‑DSS, WCAG 2.1 AA. | List legal requirements; plan for data handling and accessibility. | > **Tip:** Keep a living document (Google Docs, Notion, Confluence) so everyone stays aligned. --- ## 2️⃣ Wireframes & Prototypes | Tool | Use case | Why it helps | |------|----------|--------------| | **Figma / Sketch / Adobe XD** | Low‑to‑high fidelity wireframes | Visualise layout, navigation, and interactions early. | | **InVision / Marvel** | Interactive prototypes | Test flows with stakeholders before coding. | | **Storybook** | Component library | Build UI components in isolation; great for design hand‑off. | **Workflow:** 1. Sketch rough page layouts (Home, Category, Product Detail, Cart, Checkout, Account). 2. Add interactive hotspots for key actions (Add to Cart, Checkout, Search). 3. Validate with a quick usability test (5‑minute task completion). --- ## 3️⃣ Tech Stack Decision | Option | Pros | Cons | Typical Use‑Case | |--------|------|------|------------------| | **React + Next.js** | SSR/SSG, rich ecosystem, easy API routes | Learning curve for SSR | Most popular for e‑commerce (Shopify Hydrogen, BigCommerce). | | **Vue + Nuxt.js** | Simpler learning curve, SSR/SSG | Smaller community than React | Great for rapid MVPs. | | **Angular** | Opinionated, built‑in services, RxJS | Verbose, heavier bundle | Enterprise‑grade apps. | | **SvelteKit** | Tiny bundle, reactive syntax | Smaller ecosystem | Emerging choice for performance. | **Recommendation:** If you’re starting fresh, **React + Next.js** gives you the best balance of performance, SEO, and developer experience. If you already have a Vue or Angular background, pick the corresponding framework. --- ## 4️⃣ Project Skeleton (Next.js Example) ```bash npx create-next-app@latest ecommerce-frontend cd ecommerce-frontend npm install axios swr react-query ``` ### Folder structure ``` /components # Reusable UI components /pages # Route pages (index.tsx, product/[slug].tsx, cart.tsx, etc.) /lib # API helpers, utilities /hooks # Custom hooks (useCart, useAuth) /styles # Global CSS / Tailwind config /public # Static assets (images, icons) ``` --- ## 5️⃣ Core Features & Implementation | Feature | Key Components | Suggested Libraries | |---------|----------------|---------------------| | **Product Catalog** | `ProductList`, `ProductCard` | `react-infinite-scroll-component` | | **Search & Filters** | `SearchBar`, `FilterSidebar` | `Algolia InstantSearch` or `Fuse.js` | | **Product Detail** | `ProductDetail`, `ImageGallery`, `Reviews` | `react-image-gallery` | | **Shopping Cart** | `CartProvider`, `CartItem`, `CartSummary` | `react-use-cart` or custom context | | **Checkout Flow** | `CheckoutForm`, `PaymentGateway` | Stripe Elements, PayPal SDK | | **User Accounts** | `Login`, `Register`, `Profile` | Auth0, Firebase Auth, or custom JWT | | **Admin Dashboard** | `DashboardLayout`, `ProductTable`, `OrderTable` | Ant Design, Material‑UI | | **SEO & SSG** | `next/head`, `getStaticProps`, `getServerSideProps` | Next.js built‑in | | **State Management** | Context API or Redux Toolkit | Redux Toolkit (if global state heavy) | | **Testing** | Unit tests, E2E tests | Jest + React Testing Library, Cypress | | **Accessibility** | ARIA attributes, semantic HTML | axe-core, jest-axe | ### Example: Shopping Cart Context ```tsx // lib/cartContext.tsx import { createContext, useContext, useReducer } from 'react'; type CartItem = { id: string; name: string; price: number; quantity: number; }; type CartState = { items: CartItem[]; }; const CartContext = createContext<{ state: CartState; dispatch: React.Dispatch; }>({ state: { items: [] }, dispatch: () => null }); export const CartProvider: React.FC<{ children: React.ReactNode }> = ({ children }) => { const [state, dispatch] = useReducer(cartReducer, { items: [] }); return {children}; }; export const useCart = () => useContext(CartContext); function cartReducer(state: CartState, action: any): CartState { switch (action.type) { case 'ADD_ITEM': // logic to add item return state; case 'REMOVE_ITEM': // logic to remove item return state; default: return state; } } ``` --- ## 6️⃣ API Integration | API | How to call | Notes | |-----|-------------|-------| | **Product API** | `GET /api/products` | Use SWR or React Query for caching. | | **Cart API** | `POST /api/cart/add` | Keep cart state in localStorage for offline support. | | **Checkout API** | `POST /api/checkout` | Use serverless functions or backend microservice. | | **Auth API** | `POST /api/auth/login` | JWT stored in HttpOnly cookie. | **Example with SWR:** ```tsx import useSWR from 'swr'; import axios from 'axios'; const fetcher = (url: string) => axios.get(url).then(res => res.data); export const useProducts = () => { const { data, error } = useSWR('/api/products', fetcher); return { products: data, isLoading: !error && !data, isError: error, }; }; ``` --- ## 7️⃣ Styling & Theming | Approach | When to use | |----------|-------------| | **CSS Modules** | Small projects, isolated styles. | | **Tailwind CSS** | Rapid prototyping, utility‑first design. | | **Styled‑Components / Emotion** | Dynamic styling, theming. | | **Material‑UI / Ant Design** | Ready‑made component libraries. | **Tailwind Setup (Next.js):** ```bash npm install -D tailwindcss postcss autoprefixer npx tailwindcss init -p ``` Add to `tailwind.config.js`: ```js module.exports = { content: ['./pages/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}', './components/**/*.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}'], theme: { extend: {} }, plugins: [], }; ``` Then import in `_app.tsx`: ```tsx import '../styles/globals.css'; ``` --- ## 8️⃣ Performance Optimisation | Technique | Tool | Why it matters | |-----------|------|----------------| | **Image optimisation** | `next/image` | Automatic resizing, lazy loading. | | **Code splitting** | Next.js dynamic imports | Load only needed chunks. | | **Prefetching** | `next/link` prefetch | Faster navigation. | | **Critical CSS** | `next/font` or `styled-components` SSR | Reduces render‑blocking. | | **Bundle analysis** | `next-bundle-analyzer` | Identify heavy dependencies. | **Example: Lazy‑load a component** ```tsx import dynamic from 'next/dynamic';
